items.hook: In a model, honeybee feeding peaks at a middling lingering rate that balances recruitment and jams
items.summary: A stochastic model couples bees searching toward chemical cues with random-order service at nectar donors. Fed bees linger and strengthen the cue, which attracts more searchers but also causes crowding. Feeding is fastest at an intermediate abandonment rate, and faster donors draw more recruits. The work is theoretical and is not tested against measured colonies.
items.title: Chemotactic recruitment offsets congestion in honeybee trophallaxis

items.hook: In simulation, Mars at 30 hPa could support lichen, but breathable air would take thousands of years
items.hook_turn: but breathable air would take thousands of years

readout.label: Pressure consistent with lichen and moss

items.summary: These are the first 3-D climate simulations of a terraformed Mars with an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Temperatures at 5 times today's pressure fit lichen and moss, and forests become possible at 60 hPa. Making breathable air by photosynthesis would take at least thousands of years and more oxygen than Mars's known CO2 supplies hold. The model leaves out dust, the water cycle, and soil chemistry.
items.title: The climate and potential habitability of a warm and oxygenated Mars

items.hook: A hot Jupiter's transits vanished over seven years of TESS data, pulled off line by a hidden neighbor
items.hook_turn: pulled off line by a hidden neighbor
items.summary: TOI-2535 b is the first planet around a single star whose transits were watched disappearing, as its orbit tilted until it no longer crossed the star's disk. Seven years of TESS photometry plus radial velocities point to a Saturn-mass or larger perturber in resonance. The perturber is inferred from modeling and has not been detected directly.
items.title: A TESS Disappearing Act: The Vanishing Transits of TOI-2535 b

items.hook: A protein-evolution AI guided two lab campaigns to enzyme variants over 10 times more active than wild type
items.summary: ProTEUS is a model that predicts effects of mutations, trained on deep mutational scanning data, and uses lab feedback to steer evolution. It beat established models on mutation prediction, and its fast structure predictor runs over 10 times faster than AlphaFold3. Campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase gave variants with over 10-fold higher activity. Only two enzymes were tested.
items.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution

items.hook: A tidal disruption flare shows a carbon emission doublet for the first time, hinting at a dense envelope
items.summary: Spectra from the Very Large Telescope reveal a C IV doublet near 5800 angstroms in the off-nuclear tidal disruption event 2025abcr, a first for such events. The authors attribute it to fluorescence and photon trapping like that in Wolf-Rayet winds, which favors a compact, dense envelope. This rests on one event and a proposed mechanism not yet checked with radiative-transfer models.
items.title: Identification of the C IV $\lambda\lambda$5801, 5812 Emission in the Off-Nuclear TDE 2025abcr

items.hook: Tuza's triangle-cover bound holds for some sparse-enough graphs with at most four triangles per edge
items.summary: Tuza's conjecture says the fewest edges needed to hit every triangle is at most twice the most edge-disjoint triangles. The author proves it for graphs where each edge sits in at most four triangles, with limits on the densest edges and on average degree, using edge reductions, discharging and computer-checked certificates. A density condition is still required, and the general conjecture stays open.
items.title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture

items.hook: Thulium-169 absorbs gamma rays more strongly near its peak than earlier data and evaluations said
items.hook_turn: than earlier data and evaluations said
items.summary: Researchers measured how often thulium-169 emits a neutron after absorbing laser-Compton gamma rays, from threshold up to 14.61 MeV. Their values match earlier data below 12 MeV but are significantly higher near the peak. Feeding the updated rates into a 20 solar-mass supernova model barely changes the predicted abundances of p-nuclei, so the astrophysical impact is small.
items.title: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(\gamma,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $\gamma$-Process Calculations

items.hook: Seven qubits built a three-electron Laughlin state. Its hidden many-body coherence showed up.
items.hook_turn: Its hidden many-body coherence showed up.
items.summary: Using seven superconducting qubits, the team prepared a three-electron fractional quantum Hall state and reconstructed its full density matrix. Coherence among vortex-dressed particles extended over longer distances than electron coherence, and a quasihole showed fractional charge response and a geometric-phase signature. It is a tiny system of three electrons, so the findings are checked only against finite-size benchmarks.
items.title: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor

items.hook: German price volatility fell as wind and solar grew, but price variability across the day rose
items.hook_turn: but price variability across the day rose
items.summary: The paper separates price differences across delivery times (variability) from price changes over trading time (volatility). Using 25 years of German data and 24 European bidding zones, variability fell then rose since the 2010s and grows with solar share, while volatility declined. The evidence is descriptive, so it does not prove that wind and solar cause the shifts.
items.title: Have wind and solar energy increased electricity price volatility? And what is electricity price volatility, anyway?

items.hook: Tunneling-microscope spectra can reveal spin entanglement in nanographene chains
items.summary: The authors show that features of inelastic tunneling spectra, including the number of active transitions and their spectral moments, encode entanglement between neighboring spin-1/2 sites. Applying the relations to measured nanographene spin chains gave good agreement with theory. The links are derived for idealized spin-1/2 models, and real systems with other interactions may fit less cleanly.
items.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope

items.hook: Hyperbolic groups are either virtually free or have polygon slimness growing like log n
items.summary: The paper defines a slimness function that tracks how thin geodesic polygons are as their number of sides grows, and shows it is a quasi-isometry invariant for hyperbolic spaces. For finitely generated hyperbolic groups it is either bounded, exactly when the group is virtually free, or grows like log n. The sharp dichotomy covers hyperbolic groups only.
items.title: Slim Polygons, Hyperbolicity, and a new Quasi-Isometric Invariant

items.hook: Fluid flow does not lower the 4π mass threshold for Keller-Segel blow-up, settling an open conjecture
items.summary: In a model of cells attracted to a chemical they emit while carried by a fluid, the authors prove that every initial mass below 4π gives a unique global bounded solution in two dimensions. This answers a question left open since earlier work reached only 2π. The proof builds a new quasi-energy inequality from isoperimetric estimates and rearrangement. It covers the subcritical side and bounded planar domains only.
items.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations

items.hook: A derandomized low-degree test can fail with about q^(3/2) lines, yet works once the field is larger
items.hook_turn: yet works once the field is larger
items.summary: A low-degree test checks whether a function is close to a polynomial by looking at random lines. The authors build a function and a set of nearly q^(3/2) lines where agreement is about 1/2 on each line, yet the function is far from low-degree polynomials. They also prove the test works with O(q) lines when the field is large enough. The results cover the two-variable case only.
items.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test

items.hook: Fujita's very ampleness conjecture is proved for projective bundles over curves
items.summary: For a projective bundle over a smooth complex curve, the paper proves that the canonical bundle twisted by k ample line bundles is very ample once k is at least n+2. This settles a case of Fujita's very ampleness conjecture. It applies only to this class of bundles over curves, not to general varieties.
items.title: Fujita's Very Ampleness Conjecture for $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$-Bundles over Curves

items.hook: Most of 34 predicted compounds failed to form in the predicted structure when arc-melted
items.summary: The authors tried to make 34 ternary compounds that large databases predict to be stable, using arc melting. Most formed disordered variants or multiphase mixtures instead of the predicted structure, while four gave new ordered structures. They propose simple filters to screen out unlikely candidates. The sample is small and one synthesis method was used, so the failure rate is only a rough guide.
items.title: Experimental Evaluation of High-Throughput Structure Predictions

items.hook: A Raman-coupled potassium gas in a 1D lattice should behave as anyons, simulations show
items.hook_turn: should behave as anyons, simulations show
items.summary: The authors propose a lattice model, the Raman anyon-Hubbard model, in which laser-dressed bosons pick up phases that depend on neighboring occupation. Numerical calculations show the signatures of 1D anyons: lopsided momentum distributions, one-way-biased transport and chiral bound states. They argue 39K atoms could test it. Everything is simulation so far, with no experiment.
items.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas

items.hook: Early X-ray decay spectra separate collapsar gamma-ray bursts from merger-driven ones
items.hook_turn: separate collapsar gamma-ray bursts from merger-driven ones
items.summary: Fitting the steep X-ray decay of 23 Swift bursts from collapsing stars, the authors find that spectral peak energy and cooling frequency track luminosity along a line distinct from merger candidates. They also offer a photon index and luminosity cut for Einstein Probe transients. The collapsar sample is small, and the merger comparison relies on candidates rather than confirmed events.
items.title: Early X-ray emission as an observational diagnostic of gamma-ray burst progenitors

items.hook: A logic theory with four countable models gives F(4) equals 8, closing a gap between 7 and 8
items.summary: Earlier work showed the number of Scott complexities for theories with exactly four countable models was 7 or 8. This paper builds a sentence whose four models have four different complexities, which settles the value at 8. The construction starts from an Ehrenfeucht theory and applies Morleyization. It resolves one case only and says nothing about other model counts.
items.title: The Four-Model Scott Complexity Spectrum: $F(4)=8$

items.hook: Random encoders plus expurgation beat the best known distance for 192 qubit codes in Grassl's tables
items.hook_turn: beat the best known distance for 192 qubit codes in Grassl's tables
items.summary: The author generates random quantum error-correcting codes, then removes low-weight logical operators by promoting some to stabilizers. 192 codes exceed the listed distance by one or two, and their distances are certified exactly by exhaustive enumeration. A counting argument predicts 619 more improvements. The gains are for specific sizes and the codes are not shown to be practical to decode.
items.title: Random encoders and expurgation improve 1,873 entries of the Grassl qubit code tables

items.hook: No method with fixed function and Jacobian budgets can exceed order 2^(N_F+N_J-1), a conjecture proved
items.summary: The paper proves the Cordero-Torregrosa conjecture: for solvers that make a fixed number of function and Jacobian queries per cycle, convergence order cannot exceed 2 to the power of the total queries minus one. The proof builds one entire function and one sequence of start points that defeats every higher exponent. These are upper bounds only, and the paper does not show any budget reaches them.
items.title: Proof of the Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture for Methods with Arbitrary Rules and Its Refinement under Paired Function and Jacobian Evaluations

items.hook: Wandering continua in the Julia set of a finite-type entire function have zero area
items.summary: The paper proves a measure-theoretic companion to Sullivan's no-wandering-domain theorem. Using a conservativity theorem for maps injective on an invariant set, it also shows almost every point in the renormalization core of infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials is recurrent. The results cover finite-type entire functions and unicritical polynomials only, not general maps.
items.title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
